candidates.summary: :::details never calls Push/Pop from nestdepth.go, so nesting is unbounded and a ~180 KB realm page runs gnoweb out of memory
candidates.failure_scenario: A realm whose Render returns strings.Repeat(":::details a\n", 14000), 182 KB and under maxMarkdownRenderBytes (1 MiB, render.go:29), nests 14000 blocks. goldmark appends one lineStat per open block per line (parser.go:1106, reset only on a blank line), so memory and time grow with lines x depth: 10000 lines allocate 5.9 GiB in 2.3 s and 14000 lines crash the process with 'fatal error: runtime: out of memory' under a 6.1 GiB limit. Every visit to that page repeats it, and the crash takes gnoweb down for every user. The reviewer's 3.8 s at 20k understates it: memory runs out first. Push(pc) after parseOpenFence and Pop(pc) in Close cap it at 4 levels: 80000 lines take 96 MiB and 56 ms, and all goldens pass.

candidates.failure_scenario:
isExtDelimiter (gnovm/stdlibs/chain/markdown/markdown.go:548) matches only <gno-...> and </gno-...>, and Block already escapes headings, quotes and list markers. A user comment 'hi

candidates.summary: the first sufficient fence closes the outermost open details, unlike the pandoc convention the ADR names, so nesting only works with colon counts that strictly decrease inward
candidates.failure_scenario:
':::details A :::details B x ::: y :::' closes A and B on the first ':::', and 'y' plus the last ':::' render outside as

y :::

. Pandoc closes the innermost div. An inner block that uses more colons (':::details O ::::details I x :::: y :::') also closes both on '::::'. The ADR documents the early close but calls it pandoc's. Letting the innermost open details own a fence line (the same Continue site as candidate 2) gives pandoc nesting and keeps the more-colons trick for code.
